Confirmed. EVW p.780 supplies both steps immediately before Lemma8.9, whereas /135 only explicitly supplies Sp reduction. A map to A killed by ell^k factors uniquely through T/ell^k. In a symplectic basis h_0=diag(qI,I) has multiplier q; every finite-level multiplier-q matrix is hbar_0 sbar with sbar symplectic, so lifting sbar through the existing smooth Sp reduction gives the required fixed-multiplier lift. Confirmed as a supported-domain/source-expansion gap, not as a counterexample to positive proportions. The published abstract (p.729, also checked as an image) omits the congruence condition; p.730 explicitly discusses a different distribution when q≡1 mod ell. The displayed proof through Proposition8.3 and Theorem8.8 uses moment one and ell∤q(q−1). E11 records the characteristic restrictions but not this additional discrepancy. For A=F_ell^2 and g≥2, independent ordered covectors are classified under Sp by their alternating pairing a∈F_ell (Witt extension); all ell values occur. If q≡1 mod ell, the finite-level multiplier coset is Sp itself, so all these orbits are rational; −I preserves each. I independently enumerated the ell=3,g=2 case: three transvection orbits of sizes 1920,2160,2160. Thus the written moment-one proof cannot simply be reused. The count does not refute positive masses for the modified distribution, nor does it establish a fixed-q limiting moment: it gives a different main term, with the existing large-q error. Record the currently proved domain or supply the modified-distribution and positive-mass argument (including any required Garton input). Do not say the abstract is false or that the authors claimed CL itself at q≡1. The current arXiv listing includes the congruence restriction; the bounded search found no correction to this discrepancy and establishes no novelty claim.
